segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you've ever checked your ad account and seen Meta spending all of your ad budget on a creative that is just not getting good performance,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and you constantly ask yourself, "What is Meta doing, and why is Meta putting spend on these, quote unquote, 'bad ads'?"

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Well, in this week's video, I'm actually going to help you understand what Meta is doing, and essentially break down why Meta is spending so much money on your, again, "bad ads",

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and how you can actually use this as a learning to be able to make ads that can actually scale, and not only suck up all the spend in your ad account, but also get great performance.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And if you actually stay and watch to the end of the video, I'm actually going to show you a day-by-day example of a new super winner that we launched in one of our client ad accounts that went from essentially $0 to over $3,000 a day in spend

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: just by testing ads the way that we do, and trusting Meta to spend on ads the right way.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, with all that said, let's go ahead and jump in to this week's video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: All right. So, as you see on screen, we're inside of an ad account, and for the sake of protecting our client's data, these things are going to be blurred, but I will actually tell you whether or not these ads are the same, or what is actually happening.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But essentially, as you can see here, last month we spent about $58,000 in this one campaign specifically.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And as you can see, our top-spending ad spent about $7,500 with a return on ad spend of 1.58.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, for a lot of people, this is where it drives you crazy, because you're looking at Meta, and you're saying, "Okay, Meta, why are we spending $7,500 on this ad to get a 1.58,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: when for example, down here, we have this ad that is getting a 2.97?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Like, Meta, what are you doing? Just spend more on this ad. Why are you spending money on all these other ads that are getting a sub-2x ROAS when we could be getting a 3?"

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, the reason why Meta is not spending more on this ad, and the reason why it's actually spending more on this ad specifically, is because of one thing and one thing only, and that one thing is scale, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You have to understand that Meta is essentially a machine that wants you to spend more on ads, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And at the end of the day, it wants you, based off of the settings that you have given it, it wants to get you the highest volume of conversions at the lowest cost possible.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, the key point there is volume. Like I said, Meta wants you to scale, a.k.a., it wants you to have volume.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, by breaking this down, you can see that essentially Meta is telling us that, "Hey, I'm going to spend the most amount of budget on this ad because I believe it will get us the highest volume of purchases at the lowest cost possible."

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, does it have the lowest cost in the account? Absolutely not, but what it does have is it has the highest volume.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And a lot of the times—we're going to go through a few different accounts here—you will notice that the top-spending ad has the most amount of purchases.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And if you ask every single marketer out there that has scaled to even just, you know, $500,000 a month, or $1,000,000 a month, or for some of the brands that we work with, $10 million a month,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: they will always take a high volume of purchases over an ad that doesn't get a lot of spend and has a good-looking ROAS, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, I'm going to actually help you understand though a level deeper of why that's happening, but just know essentially Meta is trying to push for volume.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, as you can see here, you might even be looking at this ad right here, which is at a 1.97, has a $65 CPA, and as you can see, Meta only decided to spend about $3,800 on this ad.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, the question that you need to ask yourself before, in this instance, turning off your top-spending bad ad—because again, this top-spending ad is getting a 1.58x return on ad spend.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: This ad right here has a 1.97, this ad has a 1.83, and this ad has a 2.97. So, technically, I should turn this off.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, that is where you're making a colossal mistake, and a lot of the times you're actually ruining your Facebook ad performance by doing that,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because what's happening here is this ad is actually carrying essentially this entire account, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And on top of that, just from a numbers perspective, this ad right here is almost at two times the amount of scale of the next best ad.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, the question that you need to ask yourself before actually turning off your top-spending, again, in quotations, "bad ad"—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and the reason why I keep saying in quotations is because my belief is that your top-spending ad, especially if it's an ad that had performance at some point or has been validated—I will talk about specific examples where you can have ads get a lot of spend

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and not actually work at all, and so I will dive into that, but for 99% of the cases,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: for most of you guys, your top-spending ad is actually probably your best ad, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: A lot of you guys have your mindset completely wrong, where you think the top-spending ad that has a low ROAS is a bad ad. I promise you it is not.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But let's continue to dive in. So again, talking about elements of scale here, let's say we wanted to turn off this ad.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The question, what I have everybody in Evolve ask themselves, is if I was to take this $7,500, and put this $7,500 into this ad here, or even the top two ads in regards to spend,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Do I think that I would be able to get a better return on ad spend than the 1.58 that I'm getting? Well, let's just think through it.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Okay, well, here we're spending $3,800, which is essentially half of what we're spending here.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If I was to double the budget on this ad, do I think my return on ad spend would be better than a 1.58?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And for any of you who have experience actually scaling ad accounts, you know that, a lot of the times, whenever you increase budget, your ROAS goes down.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And now, the rate that it goes down is completely dependent on the ad creative itself and on the brand itself.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But in most instances, if you scale 20%, a lot of the times, your return on ad spend is going to drop anywhere from 5 to 25% as well.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, every single time you increase budget, a.k.a try to reach more people with that ad,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: the overall efficiency goes down because you're forcing Meta to show your ad to more people.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, to bring this point back home, the thing that you need to ask yourself before turning off the top-spending ad

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is, okay, well, if I know that if I increase my budget, my ROAS is going to go down,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: well, if I, in this instance, were to, let's say, triple this budget, do I think my return on ad spend would be better than a 1.58

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: if this ad right here that's getting a 1.97, and, again, half of the spend,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but because we're turning this off, we'd have to take this 7,500 and put it on this ad,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: do I think if by tripling this ad spend I would have better than a 1.58?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And if you ask me, that answer's absolutely not, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, in that instance, I'm not going to turn that off, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, that is one of the easiest ways just to figure out whether or not you should turn off a high-spending ad,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: whereas, let's take a look at this ad, for instance, which is an ad that we did actually turn off,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: where you can see it was spending $2,000, and it had a 0.78x return on ad spend.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, we turned this ad off because we were like, okay, well, this is getting a 0.78, and this $2,000 budget

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: can filter into, let's say, this ad right here that's getting a 2.97, this ad that's getting a 1.83, and this ad that's getting a 1.97,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and it's probably going to push majority of the budget up into the top-spending ad.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, do I think I could get a better return on ad spend than 0.78 by spending an extra $2,000 on this ad?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I would say so, right? That would be essentially adding close to around 25% in budget, or whatever it may be, to this ad,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and I think if I added 25% in budget to this ad right here that's getting a 1.58, it would probably do better than a 0.78.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, that is the framework that we use to essentially make decisions in the ad account

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is, okay, if I turn off this ad, and this spend has to go elsewhere, what is going to happen?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: That's why, a lot of the times, when you guys turn off these high-spending ads, or these ads that are, again, bad ads because the ROAS is low,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: meanwhile they're getting all the spend in your ad account, the rest of your account starts to do worse as a result, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, that is the first and most important thing that you need to understand, and the framework that you need to use

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is, okay, if I am to take this spend, I'm going to turn this ad off, now all of a sudden, this spend has to go into all these other ads,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: do I think it will be able to uphold that additional ad spend? And most of the time, the answer is going to be no.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, again, in some instances, like this ad here, you can see we had at $2,000 in budget, 0.78,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I'm looking at my top four ads up here, I'm like, hey, you know what? I feel like this $2,000 could be more efficiently spent on these other ads.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, then, in that instance, we'll turn it off.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, let's go ahead and take a deeper dive, though, into, for example, the second thing that I actually mentioned,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: which is around how these ads that are getting the majority of spend in your account are usually carrying the account,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: just by scrolling over slightly to frequency.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, one thing that I want you to notice here is that our frequency on this top ad is 1.89, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, what that essentially means is that people on average are seeing this 1.89 times.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, if I am scrolling through Facebook and I see this ad, I am probably going to see it a second time.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Facebook is just going to serve it to me a second time.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: That's why you need to pay attention to reach and impressions, because what this tells you

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is essentially, hey, we reached 220,000 individual people, but overall total impressions is 418,000, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, some people may have seen this four times, some people may have seen it once, but on average, the frequency is 1.89.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And now, the reason why this metric matters is because it's actually going to tell you where an ad essentially is in a funnel, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, remember that ad that was at a 2.97x, this ad right here?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Well, look at its frequency. It's

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: 3.2, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And keep in mind again volume, and keep in mind scale, this ad is getting essentially one third of the total spend that our top spending ad is getting, okay? So one third,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and it almost has two times the frequency, which means that people are being essentially retargeted with this ad, which would make sense why the 2.97 ROAS is so high.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so a lot of the times, people will also kill their top spending ads, and then all of a sudden, after maybe not one day, maybe not two days, maybe not three, but a week later, their entire ad account, and the overall ROAS, which is what matters more than anything, is going down,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and they start panicking, and they start freaking out, and it's because the ad that is doing retargeting, they don't realize is actually doing retargeting because they don't understand how to look at frequency, and as a result of that,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: the ad that was doing all the prospecting, that was getting all of the eyeballs, that was getting people into the funnel, is no longer there.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so now you have a retargeting ad, but you don't have anything that's actually getting people into the funnel for it to retarget, and so what ends up happening? Well, performance starts to go down.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And as a result of that, you now have to start prospecting, or Meta basically says like, "Hey dude, what the hell? Like, why did you turn off that ad? Like, that was my ad to go and get cold eyeballs so I could get you a high volume of purchases."

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then when you tell Meta like, "Hey, no, don't spend on that," then it's like, "Okay, well, now I've gotta find a new ad to prospect with."

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so what can end up happening is your account can start to become unstable because Meta is now having to spend on all these different ads to figure out, "Hey, what is gonna be my new prospecting ad? Like, I just lost the ad that I was prospecting with, but now I no longer have it. So now I've gotta find a new one.", okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And another thing that's super important to look at as well is cost per click. A lot of the times, we will see Meta favor top-of-funnel ads that get a very good cost per click,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and then on the inverse, you're going to see your high-ROAS, high-conversion ads usually have a higher cost per click, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: This retargeting ad has a 2.97 ROAS, but a $2.64 cost per click. Meanwhile, this ad up here that's doing slightly more prospecting has a $1.60 cost per click.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you take a look at this ad right here that is clearly also doing some prospecting, 1.75x, right, $1.18 cost per click, you can see Meta is definitely doing some prospecting with this ad as well.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so what you need to understand is what is happening in the account. If you come into your account, and you filter by purchase ROAS, and this is how you decide what your good ads are,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I mean, look at this. Some of you might be looking at like, "Oh my gosh, this ad has you know 110x ROAS," or "This ad has a 59x ROAS, like, I need to force budget on this. I need to pull this out and put this--" It's not at scale.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: It's got one purchase, okay? And so it's just not significant, okay? This ad essentially got lucky, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: We spent a dollar on this, because again, we test through CBO, which I do have an entire video on my channel, I'll have my editors pop it up, and it tells you exactly how we run our Facebook Ads using our one-campaign structure, so you can go and check that out after this video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But just to help you understand and to put this in some kind of a digestible format, cuz I know we're ping-ponging all over the place, spend is the only indicator that we ever filter by, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Spend is the number-one metric that matters most, okay? For me, and if you want to be like the actual guys that are scaling and above, or the actual brands that we scale spending millions of dollars a month on ads, we have brands spending over a million dollars a month just on one ad account, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, in this instance here, as you can see, we are filtering by spend to see, "Hey, what ads are the most scalable?" That is step number one.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Step number two is to then look at your KPI metrics, which is going to be your cost per result or your purchase return on ad spend, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then from there, you need to understand the difference between them. You need to understand, okay, well this ad is at two times the scale as this one, and although the ROAS is slightly worse than this one, this ad makes sense to keep it on because it is prospecting and it is carrying a lot of the account.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then again, by taking a look at the secondary metrics, so things like frequency, CPM, cost per click, you're going to start to get an understanding of where these ads kind of fit in the funnel.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But I also want you to understand that a lot of times your best ads also do retargeting.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: For those of you that remember, I don't even know if I made videos about this back then, but we used to have dedicated retargeting campaigns, and usually in those dedicated retargeting campaigns, ads that were doing the best in our prospecting campaigns were also doing the best in retargeting, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Because they're just great ads. And so, a lot of the times, you don't-- A lot of people think you need to have specific retargeting ads, and are some ads more retargeting than others? 100%. But the point is is Meta's gonna know better than you, which is why we run ads the way that we do.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so hopefully this helps you understand what is going on with spend. Let's get out of this ad account, and let's go take a look at another one.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: All right, cool. So as you can see, we're on screen here, and I'm now actually in the ad set level to show you how we actually test creatives. Again, we test everything through batches of ads,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but I want to show you an example here of an ad that again is absolutely murdering, okay? So the account, in this campaign specifically, is spending about 9.2k per day, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And as you can see, this ad was getting $6,800 a day in spend at a 2.03x ROAS.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, this is where some of you would be like, "Well, look at this, like, this ad's getting a 2.8, this ad's getting a 3.8. Look at this one: 17x ROAS, why are we not scaling that?" This is where you guys need to understand that again, Meta is very smart, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so there are going to be instances where yes, you actually do have other ads that start getting really good performance, and I want you to keep an eye on this row specifically to see what actually happens.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So this is August 31st. Let's go ahead and move over to September 1st.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And, as you can see, oh, wow. Meta actually spent an extra $500, or $476 on this ad set specifically, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And, as you can see, our top-spending ad lost a bit of spend. It went from $6800 in spend to 5400,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but, as you can see, Meta started pushing more spend towards this one here. And take a look, the ROAS was a 4X compared to a 2.6.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If we scroll to the right, you can see the frequency is relatively low, right? So, they're both essentially prospecting. And if we take a look at the cost per click, the cost per click is actually better on this one as well. Okay, well, that's interesting.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Let's see what happens if we go to the next day. So, we go to the next day, and, oh, look at this. Now, this ad is getting even more spend.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And, on top of that, we did have another ad start picking up spend as well, which I'm going to talk about a second. But focusing on the good here, you can see this ad now got 2.4k in spend,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: which is another $1,000 more than the previous day and had a better ROAS, with again, a low frequency, a better CPM, and a really, really good cost per click, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, in this instance here, Meta is starting to see that this is a great ad. And so, if we go to the third of the month, look at this. Meta just changed our super-winner.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so now we have a new ad starting to get majority of spend. And, as you can see, now it's gotten $3,000 a day in spend.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And if you take a look at this, we actually had another ad that Our team was on fire this week, so we got another ad that started picking up spend.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But, as you can see here, now this ad is getting the majority of the spend in the ad account. Meta pulled spend away from this one, which was the previous top performer.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then, as you can see here, Meta has another ad that it's starting to spend on. And that's what Meta does. Meta has to find statistical significance,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and has to find ads that, again, can get you the highest volume of purchases possible for the lowest cost.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And Meta can't do that unless it actually spends money on ads to figure out whether or not they're actually going to be good.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And just to be clear, what I mean by that is that Meta actually doesn't need to spend on your ads at all if it knows that they're not good, okay?

segments.text: And now, if we actually fast-forward to today, you can see this ad is actually now starting to, again, get a ton of spend. Attribution is slightly delayed on this,
